claims.object_text: median seizure course period: 6 years 6 months
claims.quote: The median seizure course period from seizure onset was 6 years 6 months.
Of 113 patients, 78% and 56% experienced seizure freedom for at least 1 year and at least 2 years respectively.

In patients younger than 5 years (n = 30), 5 to 10 years (n = 52), and older than 10 years (n = 31), 57%, 81%, and 94% experienced at least 1 year of seizure freedom, and 32%, 52%, and 84% experienced at least 2 years of seizure freedom, respectively.

claims.object_text: relapse after seizure freedom; triggers include fever and ASM reduction
claims.quote: However, 58% (65 out of 113) relapsed at least once after more than 1 year of seizure freedom without trigger exposure (40%) or because of common triggers, including fever (43%) and antiseizure medication (ASM) reduction (29%).
There was an 84% risk of seizure relapse after ASM reduction attempts.

claims.object_text: decreased likelihood of seizure freedom with early seizure onset and developmental delay
claims.quote: The likelihood of seizure freedom decreased with early age at seizure onset and developmental delay.
The disease course is characterized by relapsing-remitting seizures.

claims.object_text: caution for ASM reduction in children younger than 10 years
claims.quote: ASM reduction in children younger than 10 years old requires caution.
